To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Solvency of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de

Debt to Equity Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026] is 0.77; a deterioration from 0.22 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025].

Debt to Assets Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026] is 0.40; a deterioration from 0.16 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025].

Altman-Z score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de

Solvency of Fomento Economico Mexicano,B de

Debt to Equity Ratio of Fomento Economico Mexicano,B de for the quarter-ended 30 September 2026 [Q3/2026] is 0.50; a deterioration from 0.49 in the year-earlier period [Q3/2025].

However Fomento Economico Mexicano,B de debt to equity ratio of 0.50 compares unfavorably with the Beverages sector median of 0.27.

Debt to Assets Ratio of Fomento Economico Mexicano,B de for the quarter-ended 30 September 2026 [Q3/2026] is 0.19; an improvement from 0.20 in the year-earlier period [Q3/2025].

Interest Coverage Ratio of Fomento Economico Mexicano,B de for the quarter-ended 30 September 2026 [Q3/2026] is 3.37; improved from 3.31 in the year-earlier period [Q3/2025].

Piotroski F-Score of Fomento Economico Mexicano,B de

Fomento Economico Mexicano,B de has posted a mid-range Piotroski F-Score of 6 for the half year-ended 30 June 2025 indicating a blend of strengths and weaknesses in its financial fundamentals. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. Despite three data point being unavailable, the adjusted score provides a reliable indication that Fomento Economico Mexicano,B de may be performing well in certain areas, such as cash flow or asset efficiency, it may also be facing challenges in others-highlighting the need for closer analysis by cautious investors.

Ohlson O-Score Summary

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

For the Period Ending 31 December, 2025, Fomento Economico Mexicano,B de scores an O = -9.3902

Based on the academic Ohlson model, scores below -1.80 indicate low bankruptcy risk, scores between -1.80 and 0 fall into the moderate-risk zone, and scores above 0 signal elevated financial distress.

Altman-Z score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de scores a Z = 0.66 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025]; a deterioration from 0.91 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 0.88 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

A mixed score suggests that while Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de may be performing well in certain areas, such as cash flow or asset efficiency, it may also be facing challenges in others-highlighting the need for closer analysis by cautious investors.

To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Altman-Z score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de scores a Z = 0.66 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025]; a deterioration from 0.91 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 0.88 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

- A decrease in current assets of MX$1.5 billion (or 27.2%) from the previous quarter and MX$224.8 million (or 5.2%) from year ago to MX$4.1 billion.

- An increase in current liabilities of MX$1.8 billion (or 58.3%) from the previous quarter and MX$1.5 billion (or 45.5%) from year ago to MX$4.8 billion.

The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. A mixed score suggests that while Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de may be performing well in certain areas, such as cash flow or asset efficiency, it may also be facing challenges in others-highlighting the need for closer analysis by cautious investors.

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

Altman-Z score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de scores a Z = 1.23 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]; a deterioration from 1.24 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Beneish M-score of Wal-Mart De MexicoB. de

The Beneish model is a statistical model that uses financial ratios to determine whether it is possible that a company's earnings may have been embellished or window dressed. Because it is a probability model it is used as one of several tools by investors to mitigate risk.

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

The Mexican Open-Pit segment remains the largest contributor, generating $2,511.9 million in the second quarter of 2026, or 57.6% of the segment total. The Mexican Open-Pit segment contributed 61.4% of total operating income, underscoring its central role in the Company's profitability.

Copper remains the dominant product, generating $3,116.8 million, or 72.7% of consolidated net sales in Q2 2026. Copper revenue rose 37.9% year-over-year, driven by higher LME prices (+39.8%) and COMEX prices (+30.5%), despite a 1.5% decline in copper sales volumes. Molybdenum contributed $475.8 million, or 11.1% of net sales, with prices averaging $29.44 per pound, up 43.1%. Silver posted the strongest percentage growth among products at 86.1%, reaching $375.8 million, or 8.8% of net sales, as prices surged 118.6% to $73.49 per ounce. Zinc contributed $152.2 million, or 3.5% of net sales, with prices up 30.8%. Other products, including gold and sulfuric acid, rose 50.4% to $168.3 million. On a six-month basis, copper generated $6,099.4 million (71.4% of net sales), molybdenum $921.3 million (10.8%), silver $907.3 million (10.6%), and zinc $297.2 million (3.5%). The by-product revenue stream, particularly from molybdenum and silver, significantly reduced operating cash costs net of by-product revenues to $0.05 per pound in Q2 2026, compared to $0.63 per pound in Q2 2025.

Copper remains the dominant product, generating $3,116.8 million, or 72.7% of consolidated net sales in Q2 2026. Copper revenue rose 37.9% year-over-year, driven by higher LME prices (+39.8%) and COMEX prices (+30.5%), despite a 1.5% decline in copper sales volumes. Molybdenum contributed $475.8 million, or 11.1% of net sales, with prices averaging $29.44 per pound, up 43.1%. Silver posted the strongest percentage growth among products at 86.1%, reaching $375.8 million, or 8.8% of net sales, as prices surged 118.6% to $73.49 per ounce. Zinc contributed $152.2 million, or 3.5% of net sales, with prices up 30.8%. Other products, including gold and sulfuric acid, rose 50.4% to $168.3 million. On a six-month basis, copper generated $6,099.4 million (71.4% of net sales), molybdenum $921.3 million (10.8%), silver $907.3 million (10.6%), and zinc $297.2 million (3.5%). The by-product revenue stream, particularly from molybdenum and silver, significantly reduced operating cash costs net of by-product revenues to $0.05 per pound in Q2 2026, compared to $0.63 per pound in Q2 2025.

SECTION 1: BIOGRAPHY: RAUL REVUELTA MUSALEM, CEO

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.

When does the Irresistible Sale 2026 start? The campaign kicked off on Thursday, November 5, at around 12:01 a.m. (central Mexico time) on the online stores of Walmart, Bodega Aurrera, and Sam's Club. In physical stores, it began approximately at 8:00 a.m. (central Mexico time), although the timing varied at some locations depending on their proximity. When does the Irresistible Sale 2026 end? This campaign will last for 14 days, allowing all customers of Walmart, Bodega Aurrera, and Sam's Club to take advantage of significant promotions on groceries, electronics, appliances, toys, household cleaning products, pet food, and many other items. The Irresistible Sale will conclude on Wednesday, November 18, around midnight for online stores and approximately at 10:00 p.m. for physical stores. Where can you check all the promotions from Walmart for the Irresistible Sale? The complete list of participating products is available on Walmart Mexico's official website. Availability may vary depending on the day you check, as well as the items that are on promotion. If you're interested in purchasing an item or want to check prices and availability, you can do so from the following link: https://www.walmart.com.mx/content/especiales/fin-irresistible/360013_360186 It's worth noting that this year, Walmart has launched payment options: - Up to 65% savings on selected products. - 24 months without interest with participating banks. - Start payment in February with 6 months interest-free in-store. - 1 month of free shipping with Walmart Plus. Where can you check the promotions from Aurrera? Bodega Aurrera has set up an official page for its customers to check discounted items at its locations during this season. You can access the catalog via the link: https://www.bodegaaurrera.com.mx/content/eventos/fin-irresistible-bodega/490004_610001 The supermarket also introduced payment options with participating banks: - Up to 65% savings on selected products. - Up to 24 months without interest with participating banks. - Up to 20% cashback with participating banks. Where can you check the promotions from Sam's Club? The promotions from Sam's Club are available on its e-commerce site. You can consult them at the following address: https://www.sams.com.mx/content/fin-irresistible/1330001 Please note that to access these offers, a store membership is required, which also includes special discounts for the event: - 65% off on televisions and up to 24 months without interest. - 40% off on telephony, computing, appliances, and up to 24 months without interest. - 35% off on household appliances and up to 24 months without interest. - 30% off on consoles and up to 9 months without interest.

ORIGINAL ANNOUNCEMENT [Text]

MONTREAL, Nov. 10, 2026 -- Midland Exploration Inc. (Midland) (TSX-V: MD) is pleased to announce the start of an airborne gravity gradiometer geophysical survey on the La Peltrie project, in northern Abitibi in the Detour area. The La Peltrie project is operated by Fresnillo Canada (Fresnillo), is owned 50% by Fresnillo and 50% by Midland, and consists of 540 exclusive exploration rights (EER) covering an area of 291 square kilometres.

Highlights:

Start of a 5,165 line-kilometres airborne gravity gradiometer survey on the La Peltrie project, covering the entire project, including the 2022-2023 Cu-Au-Ag-Mo mineralization intersected by drilling (see press release by Midland dated January 23, 2024).

The airborne gravity gradiometer geophysical survey will be conducted by XCalibur using their FALCON AGG system for a total of 5,165-line kilometres and covering entirely the project, including the 2022-2023 copper-gold-silver-molybdenum (Cu-Au-Ag-Mo) mineralization intersected by drilling (see press release by Midland dated January 23, 2024). High-resolution magnetic data collection is included in the system. The objective of this survey is to refine the geological and structural knowledge of the project by having a better understanding of the bedrock geology underlying important areas of glacial deposit cover. The gravity gradiometer survey detects differences in rock density and can potentially map the lithological packages present on the project.

This survey will provide further geological data which will be used to generate new exploration targets in the Cu-Au-Ag-Mo mineralization area, and also for gold at the project scale. Results are pending.

La Peltrie Project

The La Peltrie project is located 15 kilometres southeast of Agnico Eagles Zone 58N gold deposit and approximately 25 kilometres west of the former Selbaie mine. The 2022 Cu-Au-Ag-Mo mineralization intersected by drilling was extended in 2023 (see press release by Midland dated January 23, 2024). In 2024, a MMI soil sampling program totalizing 768 samples was completed at the spacing of 50-100 metres and along lines separated at 200-400 metres. The grid covers the Cu-Au-Ag-Mo mineralization area and extends northward to the southern contact with the Carheil intrusion (see press release by Midland dated December 10, 2024). In 2025, a second MMI soil sampling program totalizing 889 samples was completed on the project.

The soil sampling program successfully identified the Cu-Au-Ag-Mo mineralization area and also suggests extension towards the west. Some anomalies correlate with IP anomalies from the geophysical survey conducted in March 2024 and have yet to be drill-tested. Moreover, SRK Consulting performed a structural analysis of the high-resolution aeromagnetic survey conducted in 2020 to improve the structural and geological understanding of the copper mineralized zone.

Cautionary statements

The true thickness of reported drilling mineralization cannot be determined with the information currently available.

Mineralization occurring at deposits and former mines mentioned in this press release is not necessarily indicative of mineralization that may be intersected on projects held by Midland described in this press release.

About Midland

Midland targets the mineral potential of Quebec to make the discovery of new deposits of gold and critical metals. Midland is proud to count on reputable partners such as Fresnillo plc, Rio Tinto Exploration Canada Inc., BHP Canada Inc., Centerra Gold Inc., Barrick Mining Corporation., Agnico Eagle Mines Limited, Wallbridge Mining Company Ltd, Electric Elements Mining Corp., SOQUEM Inc., Nunavik Mineral Exploration Fund, and Abcourt Mines Inc. Midland prefers to work in partnership and intends to quickly conclude additional agreements in regard to newly acquired properties. Management is currently reviewing other opportunities and projects to build up Midlands portfolio and generate shareholder value.

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. Altman-Z score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de scores a Z = 0.73 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]; a deterioration from 1.1 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

The Beneish model is a statistical model that uses financial ratios to determine whether it is possible that a company's earnings may have been embellished or window dressed. Because it is a probability model it is used as one of several tools by investors to mitigate risk.

The Beneish M-score is calculated by using 8 key metrics:

Days Sales in Receivables Index

Gross Margin Index

Sales Growth Index

Sales General and Administrative Expenses Index

Leverage Index

Total Accruals to Total Assets Index

However an M-score greater than -1.78 suggests there could be modifications to its earnings that have occurred to help window dress the headline earnings. Currently about 16 International Depository Receipts companies have a Beneish M-score greater than -1.78.

To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Ohlson O-Score Summary

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

For the Period Ending 31 December, 2025, Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de scores an O = -9.6448

Based on the academic Ohlson model, scores below -1.80 indicate low bankruptcy risk, scores between -1.80 and 0 fall into the moderate-risk zone, and scores above 0 signal elevated financial distress.

Piotroski F-Score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de has posted a mid-range Piotroski F-Score of 6 for the half year-ended 30 June 2025 indicating a blend of strengths and weaknesses in its financial fundamentals. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. Despite one data point being unavailable, the adjusted score provides a reliable indication that Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de may be performing well in certain areas, such as cash flow or asset efficiency, it may also be facing challenges in others-highlighting the need for closer analysis by cautious investors.

Solvency of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de

Debt to Equity Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026] is 0.77; a deterioration from 0.22 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025].

Debt to Assets Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026] is 0.40; a deterioration from 0.16 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025].

Altman-Z score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de scores a Z = 0.73 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]; a deterioration from 1.1 in the year-earlier period [Q1/2025]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Beneish M-score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de

The Beneish model is a statistical model that uses financial ratios to determine whether it is possible that a company's earnings may have been embellished or window dressed. Because it is a probability model it is used as one of several tools by investors to mitigate risk.

The Beneish M-score is calculated by using 8 key metrics:

Days Sales in Receivables Index

Gross Margin Index

Asset Quality Index

Sales Growth Index

Depreciation Index

Sales General and Administrative Expenses Index

Leverage Index

Total Accruals to Total Assets Index

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de has a Beneish M-Score of -4.88 for the quarter-ended 31 March 2026 [Q1/2026]. An M-score of less than -1.78 is considered normal. However an M-score greater than -1.78 suggests there could be modifications to its earnings that have occurred to help window dress the headline earnings. Currently about 16 International Depository Receipts companies have a Beneish M-score greater than -1.78.

Zmijewski X-Score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de

For the period ending 31 December, 2025, Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste de's X-Score is -2.1283, corresponding to an estimated probability of bankruptcy of 1.67% which falls within the safe zone (X <= -1.0), indicating a very low probability of bankruptcy and reflecting a strong and stable financial position.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de has posted a mid-range Piotroski F-Score of 4 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025], indicating a blend of strengths and weaknesses in its financial fundamentals. Altman-Z score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de with all three variations.

A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Some of the most prominent supermarkets in Mexico, such as Walmart, Grupo Comercial Chedraui, and La Comer, are preparing for a gradual reduction in the weekly work hours with measures that include everything from digital strategies to reduced hours in some of their stores.

Walmart de México y Centroamérica, the largest supermarket company in the country, has been applying pilot programs since last year to incorporate reduced work hours.

At the same time, the retail giant is working on the implementation of digital price tags on shelves in several of its formats, including 100 Walmart Express stores. The goal is to extend this strategy to over 200 stores during the first half of 2027 to reduce operational costs in light of changes such as the shorter work hours and the increase in the minimum wage.

"Our operational costs increase every year. We anticipate a 12% increase in the minimum wage next year. Additionally, we will face labor reform, which involves reducing the workweek from 48 to 40 hours, starting with 46 hours next year," said Cristian Barrientos, President and CEO of Walmart de México y Centroamérica, during a call with analysts and investors regarding the company's financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Moreover, the chain is implementing projects related to smart merchandise receiving while also opening a new distribution center in the Bajío region, whose automation will enhance product management accuracy, ultimately helping to control operational costs next year amidst these labor changes.

Chedraui adopts reduced work hours

Amidst this landscape, Walmart is not the only company testing reduced work hours; Chedraui is in a similar situation and is alsorunning pilot programs involving shortened hours.

According to company advertisements, the store is hiring "B cashiers," for reduced shifts, in one of its locations in southern Mexico City, along with "A cashiers," who will work eight-hour shifts. However, the company has yet to decide whether it will implement this strategy in other stores, as it depends on the results of this trial.

Likewise, the company has been working to strengthen employee skills to achieve better store structures and make operations more efficient.

Despite these labor cost challenges, the company does not expect a decrease in its margins and profitability next year.

"We were aware of the reduction in the weekly work hours and were prepared for it. It is nothing new for next year. Therefore, we believe we are ready. We think the slowdown in consumption will continue, but the base we have already established this year will always remain," added José Antonio Chedraui Eguia, the retailer's director, during a quarterly financial conference.

Chedraui operates 755 stores in Mexico, not including 17 stores from a joint investment in the Smart & Final format in the country, according to information as of September 30, 2026.

La Comer focuses on optimizing shifts in its stores

In the case of La Comer, the company is undertaking projects to optimize staff shifts at its stores.

"Regarding labor costs, we are progressing in implementing the new legislation related to the reduction of weekly work hours," said Rogelio Garza, Director of Administration and Finance at La Comer, during a conference with analysts and investors regarding the company's financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Similarly, the retailer—established about a decade ago after the sale of Comercial Mexicana stores to Soriana—hopes to significantly mitigate this impact through shift optimization and new projects it is implementing.

La Comer operates 96 stores in the country, including City Market, Fresko, La Comer, Sumesa, and City Market Café formats, according to the company's financial information for the third quarter of 2026.

Soriana introduces self-checkout and AI in response to labor costs

Meanwhile, Soriana declined to provide details on the measures it is taking, if any, to address the reduction in work hours. However, the company has previously stated that it is implementing measures in response to rising labor costs.

The company installed600 self-checkout kiosks , which provide "significant savings in terms of personnel," explained Rodrigo Benet, the company's Chief Financial Officer, during a quarterly call with analysts and investors.

Additionally, the retailer has also incorporated artificial intelligence tools to automate certain processes.

"Previously, we had about 40 people at headquarters responsible for all personnel registration… Now, basically, everything is done by artificial intelligence with just two people. We have achieved a significant reduction in personnel merely in that process," noted Benet.

Regarding the workweek, the company responded to EL CEO that it reiterates "our commitment to complying with current labor legislation and the well-being of our teams."

The retailer reported 801 supermarket locations in the third quarter of 2026, in addition to 15 Sodimac units.

In this way, supermarkets in Mexico face a landscape of labor changes, including the reduction of the weekly work hours.

CIUDAD DE MÉXICO, 18 nov (Reuters) - Industrias Peñoles firmó un contrato de suministro de energía renovable a 20 años con Atlas Renewable Energy, que respaldará parte de la demanda eléctrica de las operaciones de la minera mexicana en el norte del país.

El proyecto, previsto para iniciar operaciones en el primer semestre de 2029 en el estado Coahuila, combinará 269 MWp de capacidad solar con un sistema de baterías y suministrará cerca de 550 GWh anuales, según un comunicado.

El acuerdo incluye energía renovable, certificados de energía limpia y potencia. El suministro permitirá a Industrias Peñoles evitar unas 244,000 toneladas anuales de dióxido de carbono equivalente.

Atlas señaló que el contrato representa su primer acuerdo de energía renovable con un cliente privado en México, tras una serie de proyectos previamente vinculados a la estatal Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE).

(Reporte de Noé Torres)

Sep 09, 2026: Derek Gaskins Takes Marketing Helm at OXXO USA

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

In his new position at OXXO USA, a subsidiary of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), Gaskins will play a pivotal role in shaping the brand's commercial strategy in the U.S. market. He will report directly to CEO Jaime Longoria and oversee a wide array of functions including marketing, merchandising, foodservice, brand development, and supplier partnerships. Gaskins expressed enthusiasm for the role, stating, 'It's one of the most exciting scopes I've had in my career.'

OXXO, which boasts over 26,000 stores globally, has recently made its foray into the United States, acquiring 249 stores from Delek US in October 2024. As OXXO seeks to build a neighborhood-relevant, food-forward convenience experience, Gaskins is expected to harness his extensive industry experience to drive growth. He noted, 'They are trying to build something meaningful here—and they asked me to help lead that commercial effort.'

Prior to this role, Gaskins held positions at Hotel Chocolat and bp, where he focused on enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency. His background includes significant tenures at various convenience retail brands, positioning him as a seasoned leader in the sector. Gaskins remarked, 'OXXO represents something I could not responsibly say no to,' highlighting the strategic importance of this opportunity.

As OXXO USA prepares to establish a stronger foothold in the U.S., Gaskins emphasized the brand's commitment to earning its place in the market. He noted, 'FEMSA came to stay, and they are bringing global best practices, significant capital, and a proven operating model.' With Gaskins at the helm of marketing, OXXO USA is poised to become a serious contender in the competitive convenience store landscape.

Argosy Investors has recently highlighted Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FMX) as a key holding in its Q1 2026 investor letter. The letter, made available on June 8th, 2026, outlines a cautious approach toward investment amid a transformative landscape characterized by an AI capital expenditure boom.

In the letter, Argosy expressed skepticism regarding the sustainability of earnings for market participants and suppliers during this capex surge. The firm emphasized the challenge of balancing supply and demand, especially given the rapid advancement of AI technologies. As companies experience rising volumes and prices, there is a growing concern that earnings could be overstated if supply ramps up faster than anticipated. Despite these concerns, Argosy has identified Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. as a viable investment option.

Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V., a prominent global franchise bottler of Coca-Cola beverages, closed at $122.88 per share on June 5th, 2026. The company's stock has seen a modest decline of 0.19% over the past month, though it enjoyed a robust gain of 17.29% over the past year. With a market capitalization of $41.86 billion, Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. remains a significant player in the beverage industry.

Argosy Investors revealed its strategic move of selling shares in Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOF) to reallocate funds into Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. The firm expressed confidence in FMX's exposure to Coca-Cola, noting the synergistic benefits of expanding convenience store operations alongside increasing beverage sales in Mexico. This pivot underscores Argosy's belief in the growth potential of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. in a rapidly evolving market.

While Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. is not currently among the most popular stocks held by hedge funds, it still garners attention. Argosy Investors remains optimistic about FMX, even as it acknowledges that certain AI stocks may present greater upside potential and lower downside risk.

SECTION 6 CORPORATE PROFILE

6.1 Activities

Fomento Económico Mexicana S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages through its Coca-Cola FEMSA subsidiary, which operates as one of the world's largest Coca-Cola franchisees. The company also manages a vast retail network, including the OXXO convenience store chain, which dominates Mexico's retail landscape and extends into select international markets. Additionally, FEMSA operates in logistics, fuel retailing, and health sciences. The fastest-growing segments include retail, driven by the aggressive expansion of OXXO stores and digital initiatives that enhance customer convenience, as well as beverage operations in emerging markets, fueled by rising consumer demand for non-alcoholic drinks and strategic acquisitions. This diversified approach has positioned FEMSA as a resilient player in the global consumer goods sector, emphasizing innovation and sustainability. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 5th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Sep 09, 2026: Derek Gaskins Takes Marketing Helm at OXXO USA

Derek Gaskins is set to re-enter the convenience-store sector, joining OXXO USA as vice president of marketing and category management. The move will take effect in mid-September, 2026, specifically on the 13th of that month, as Gaskins confirmed in an interview with CSP Daily News.

In his new position at OXXO USA, a subsidiary of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), Gaskins will play a pivotal role in shaping the brand's commercial strategy in the U.S. market. He will report directly to CEO Jaime Longoria and oversee a wide array of functions including marketing, merchandising, foodservice, brand development, and supplier partnerships. Gaskins expressed enthusiasm for the role, stating, 'It's one of the most exciting scopes I've had in my career.'

OXXO, which boasts over 26,000 stores globally, has recently made its foray into the United States, acquiring 249 stores from Delek US in October 2024. As OXXO seeks to build a neighborhood-relevant, food-forward convenience experience, Gaskins is expected to harness his extensive industry experience to drive growth. He noted, 'They are trying to build something meaningful here—and they asked me to help lead that commercial effort.'

Prior to this role, Gaskins held positions at Hotel Chocolat and bp, where he focused on enhancing customer experience and operational efficiency. His background includes significant tenures at various convenience retail brands, positioning him as a seasoned leader in the sector. Gaskins remarked, 'OXXO represents something I could not responsibly say no to,' highlighting the strategic importance of this opportunity.

As OXXO USA prepares to establish a stronger foothold in the U.S., Gaskins emphasized the brand's commitment to earning its place in the market. He noted, 'FEMSA came to stay, and they are bringing global best practices, significant capital, and a proven operating model.' With Gaskins at the helm of marketing, OXXO USA is poised to become a serious contender in the competitive convenience store landscape.

Jun 08, 2026: Argosy Investors Pivot to Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. for Stability

Argosy Investors has recently highlighted Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. (FMX) as a key holding in its Q1 2026 investor letter. The letter, made available on June 8th, 2026, outlines a cautious approach toward investment amid a transformative landscape characterized by an AI capital expenditure boom.

In the letter, Argosy expressed skepticism regarding the sustainability of earnings for market participants and suppliers during this capex surge. The firm emphasized the challenge of balancing supply and demand, especially given the rapid advancement of AI technologies. As companies experience rising volumes and prices, there is a growing concern that earnings could be overstated if supply ramps up faster than anticipated. Despite these concerns, Argosy has identified Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. as a viable investment option.

Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V., a prominent global franchise bottler of Coca-Cola beverages, closed at $122.88 per share on June 5th, 2026. The company's stock has seen a modest decline of 0.19% over the past month, though it enjoyed a robust gain of 17.29% over the past year. With a market capitalization of $41.86 billion, Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. remains a significant player in the beverage industry.

Argosy Investors revealed its strategic move of selling shares in Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOF) to reallocate funds into Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. The firm expressed confidence in FMX's exposure to Coca-Cola, noting the synergistic benefits of expanding convenience store operations alongside increasing beverage sales in Mexico. This pivot underscores Argosy's belief in the growth potential of Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. in a rapidly evolving market.

While Fomento Economico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V. is not currently among the most popular stocks held by hedge funds, it still garners attention. The number of hedge funds holding FMX decreased from 16 to 13 in the last quarter, signaling a shift in investment strategies. Argosy Investors remains optimistic about FMX, even as it acknowledges that certain AI stocks may present greater upside potential and lower downside risk.

May 19, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Expands Operational Footprint with Strategic Investments

Mexico City, May 19, 2026. Coca-Cola FEMSA, the world's largest bottler by sales volume of the Coca-Cola System, continues to strengthen its leadership in Latin America through strategic investments that expand its production capacity, modernize its infrastructure and strengthen its operating platform in the region. The date of this announcement is 2026-05-20 12:12:26.321290.

Ian Craig, CEO of Coca-Cola FEMSA, emphasized the company's commitment to disciplined and long-term investments aimed at enhancing capabilities and ensuring consistent growth. "We are investing with discipline and a long-term vision to strengthen our capabilities and ensure consistent growth in the region, always close to our customers and consumers," Craig stated. This forward-looking approach aligns with Coca-Cola FEMSA's objective of optimizing its supply chain and better serving consumer preferences.

The investment strategy is designed to reaffirm Coca-Cola FEMSA's regional leadership and its adaptability in a competitive market. By focusing on sustainable growth, the company aims to drive a robust business model that is resilient to future challenges within Latin America. This strategic direction positions Coca-Cola FEMSA favorably as it seeks to meet the evolving demands of consumers across the region.

Coca-Cola FEMSA operates across several key markets, including Mexico, Brazil, Guatemala, Colombia, and Argentina, as well as in several Central American countries. The company boasts a significant operational scale, with over 90,000 employees and annual sales of approximately 4.2 billion unit cases through more than 2.1 million outlets. Its extensive network of 55 manufacturing plants and 256 distribution centers underscores its commitment to generating economic, social, and environmental value for stakeholders throughout the value chain.

In addition to its operational expansions, Coca-Cola FEMSA is recognized for its commitment to sustainability and corporate responsibility. The company is a member of various sustainability indices, including the Dow Jones MILA Pacific Alliance Sustainability Index and the MSCI ACWI Index, reflecting its dedication to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices. As Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to grow, its strategic investments and operational enhancements are expected to play a crucial role in solidifying its leadership position in the beverage industry across Latin America.

Jul 09, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA: A Hidden Gem in Consumer Staples

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. (KOF) is emerging as a potentially undervalued opportunity in the consumer staples sector. As of 9th July 2026, the company stands as the largest Coca-Cola bottler worldwide by sales volume, serving over 270 million consumers throughout Latin America with a diverse product range that includes sparkling beverages, water, juices, sports drinks, and dairy products.

Despite operating in a mature and competitive consumer staples industry, Coca-Cola FEMSA's current market valuation suggests that investors may be overlooking its resilient cash flows and strong profitability. The company's extensive distribution network and established brand portfolio provide a competitive edge, enabling it to generate recurring cash flow.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's intrinsic value-to-price (IV/P) ratio stands at 1.50, indicating that the stock may be trading below conservative intrinsic value estimates. The firm maintains a strong free cash flow of about MXN 24.2 billion, showcasing its capability to support dividends, investments, and strategic acquisitions.

The company's financial health is further illustrated by its balance sheet, which lists total assets at approximately MXN 314.5 billion and total liabilities at around MXN 160.5 billion, resulting in a solid shareholders' equity of about MXN 154.0 billion. Despite slight increases in leverage due to acquisitions, Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to exhibit strong cash generation, enabling it to navigate macroeconomic challenges such as currency volatility and inflation.

While market concerns such as slowing consumer spending and rising commodity costs persist, Coca-Cola FEMSA's fundamentals remain compelling. With an Acquirer's Multiple of 4.0 and robust operating margins, the company appears to be a promising long-term investment for value-seeking investors looking at the consumer staples sector.

Jul 05, 2026: Coca-Cola Femsa Expands Beverage Operations for Long-Term Growth

Coca-Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume, continues to leverage its wide Latin American footprint and franchise agreements to drive beverage distribution and long-term growth opportunities. As of the 5th of July, 2026, Coca-Cola Femsa's operations underline a robust business model focused on efficiency and localized strategies that resonate with regional consumer preferences.

Coca-Cola Femsa oversees a broad network of bottling plants and distribution centers that support a high-frequency, high-volume beverage business in both emerging and developed Latin American economies. Its territories include key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and other countries in Central and South America, where population density and urbanization provide a large consumer base for ready-to-drink beverages. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

The company operates under long-term franchise and bottling agreements that define its rights and obligations to produce, market, and sell Coca-Cola branded beverages in assigned territories. Within this framework, Coca-Cola Femsa focuses on operational efficiency, portfolio management, and local commercial strategies while coordinating with the brand owner on marketing and innovation. This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. The company adapts flavors, package sizes, and multipack configurations to local consumer tastes and price points, ensuring a tailored approach that meets diverse market demands. Packaging innovation plays a central role in Coca-Cola Femsa's operations, as the company strives to meet sustainability expectations and improve efficiency.

From an investor perspective, Coca-Cola Femsa is often viewed as a consumer staples business with exposure to multiple Latin American currencies and macroeconomic environments. Analysts closely monitor capital expenditure commitments, leverage metrics, and dividend policies when assessing the balance between growth investment and shareholder returns. For many global investors, Coca-Cola Femsa represents an opportunity to tap into Latin American consumer trends through a well-established beverage platform tied to iconic soft drink brands.

Jun 23, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Launches 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle to Enhance Family Consumption

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle, targeting family consumption in key Mexican markets. This launch, taking place on 23rd June 2026, is a significant step in the company's strategy to enhance the availability of reusable packaging solutions.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

Jun 15, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA's Returnable Glass Bottle: A Timeless Choice for Latin American Consumers

Coca-Cola FEMSA's standardized returnable glass bottle remains a core workhorse in Latin America, combining refillable packaging with industrial-scale distribution. As of 15th June 2026, the bottle continues to play a vital role, particularly in Mexico and Brazil, where refillable containers are a staple of consumer habits.

The Coca-Cola returnable glass bottle is typically available in familiar single-serve formats ranging from 235 ml to 355 ml, as well as larger family sizes such as 1.0 liter and 1.25 liters. These offerings are tailored to local preferences, making them more appealing to consumers in different markets. Beyond its nostalgic appeal, the refillable glass format serves a practical purpose in Coca-Cola FEMSA's packaging mix, providing a robust container that can endure multiple wash-and-refill cycles on industrial bottling lines.

The returnable glass bottle operates on a deposit-return system, where consumers pay a deposit upon purchase and reclaim it when they return the empty bottle. This model encourages recycling and reinforces Coca-Cola FEMSA's commitment to sustainability. In the markets where Coca-Cola FEMSA operates, these bottles are commonly found in traditional trade outlets, including neighborhood stores, small groceries, and food-service channels, coexisting alongside one-way PET bottles and cans.

For Coca-Cola FEMSA, the returnable glass bottle is not merely a product but a strategic asset that caters to price-sensitive consumers while enhancing the company's sustainability narrative around refillable packaging. As of 13th June 2026, shares of Coca-Cola FEMSA (US1912411089) were trading at $105.08 on the NYSE, reflecting investor confidence in the company's enduring packaging strategies.

Over the years, Coca-Cola FEMSA has adapted its returnable glass bottle to meet evolving consumer needs and preferences. With a longstanding presence in the market, this packaging format continues to resonate with everyday soft-drink consumers in Latin America, particularly among price-conscious households and small food-service operators. The combination of tradition and practicality ensures that Coca-Cola FEMSA's returnable glass bottle remains a relevant and cherished choice.

May 19, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Amplifies Market Presence with Strategic Investments

Mexico City, May 19, 2026. Coca-Cola FEMSA, the world's largest bottler by sales volume of the Coca-Cola System, continues to strengthen its leadership in Latin America through strategic investments that expand its production capacity, modernize its infrastructure, and strengthen its operating platform in the region. The company is making significant investments aimed at reinforcing its market position and enhancing operational efficiency.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, Ian Craig, emphasized the company's commitment to disciplined investment with a long-term vision. He stated, "We are investing with discipline and a long-term vision to strengthen our capabilities and ensure consistent growth in the region, always close to our customers and consumers." This approach reflects Coca-Cola FEMSA's focus on optimizing its supply chain and adapting to consumer preferences, thereby enhancing its overall service delivery.

The strategic investment initiatives by Coca-Cola FEMSA are designed to reinforce its regional leadership and ensure sustainable growth. By optimizing production processes and modernizing facilities, the company aims to create a robust operating model that is both future-proof and aligned with market demands. This commitment to operational excellence is crucial as Coca-Cola FEMSA navigates the dynamic beverage landscape in Latin America.

With a workforce of over 90,000 employees, Coca-Cola FEMSA operates 55 manufacturing plants and 256 distribution centers, serving more than 268 million consumers annually. The company's extensive reach across Mexico, Brazil, Guatemala, Colombia, and Argentina, as well as its operations in Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Panama, Uruguay, and Venezuela, further solidifies its status as a key player in the region's beverage market.

Coca-Cola FEMSA is also recognized for its commitment to sustainability, being a member of several prestigious indices, including the Dow Jones MILA Pacific Alliance Sustainability Index and the FTSE4Good Emerging Index. These recognitions highlight the company's dedication to generating economic, social, and environmental value for its stakeholders, reinforcing its reputation as a socially responsible leader in the beverage industry.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.

6.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

Jul 06, 2026: America Movil ADR: A Gateway to Latin America's Telecom Expansion

America Movil (Class L ADR) offers investors a significant opportunity to tap into one of Latin America's largest telecom groups, providing extensive exposure to mobile, fixed-line, and broadband services across multiple markets. As of the 6th of July, 2026, the ADR allows US investors to participate in the company's operations through a New York-listed instrument that tracks its Class L shares in Mexico.

With a robust telecom footprint, America Movil operates various segments across Latin America, including mobile voice, data services, broadband internet, and fixed-line connectivity for both residential and business clients. The company has systematically expanded its market presence by investing in mobile networks, acquiring spectrum, and enhancing its service offerings in response to growing data consumption across key regions.

The ADR structure provides a simplified investment pathway for US investors, allowing them to engage with America Movil's performance via a depositary receipt rather than needing to purchase shares directly in the local market. This arrangement not only facilitates smoother currency conversions but also streamlines custody for US-based investment portfolios, making it an attractive option for those looking to diversify their holdings.

America Movil's core business model revolves around delivering diverse connectivity and related services to a wide-ranging customer base across several Latin American countries, often under well-established local brands. Its portfolio includes various offerings, from prepaid mobile plans to bundled broadband packages and digital services catering to the rising demand for streaming, cloud solutions, and enterprise connectivity.

Trading in US dollars, the America Movil Class L ADR presents a compelling opportunity for investors seeking exposure to an influential emerging-markets telecom group. The stock's pricing and liquidity reflect both the performance of its Latin American operations and the broader market sentiment surrounding telecommunications and emerging markets as an asset class, positioning America Movil as a noteworthy option for potential investors.

Jun 22, 2026: America Movil's Claro Box TV: A New Era for 4K Streaming

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its latest innovation, the Claro Box TV, which transforms any HDMI screen into a 4K streaming hub. This compact device, launched on 22nd June 2026, provides seamless access to popular platforms such as Claro Video, Netflix, and YouTube, all navigable via a lightweight, voice-capable remote control.

Claro Box TV is designed for broadband customers in Latin America, offering a convergence of pay TV channels and major streaming apps within a single HDMI device. The system operates on a customized Android TV interface, allowing users to download additional applications from the Google Play Store, including Disney+, Prime Video, and Spotify, alongside pre-installed offerings like Claro Video and YouTube.

Installation is user-friendly; users simply connect one cable to their router and another to their TV, with Wi-Fi connectivity available for those who prefer it. The Bluetooth remote is equipped with dedicated buttons for Netflix and Claro Video, and features voice search capabilities via Google Assistant, contributing to an intuitive user experience.

America Movil's Claro Box TV aims to bolster its broadband customer retention strategy by integrating traditional TV channels with streaming capabilities in a single interface. This approach is particularly beneficial in markets such as Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, where the box not only provides access to live channels but also offers an electronic program guide, minimizing the need to switch inputs during viewing.

As America Movil continues to expand its reach, the Claro Box TV serves as a strategic asset in reducing customer churn in fixed-line broadband services. By controlling both the network and the viewing interface, America Movil can promote its own content alongside partnerships, ensuring a direct relationship with viewers and enhancing its competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

Jun 16, 2026: America Movil Simplifies Offerings with Telcel Max Sin Limite Plan

America Movil's Telcel Max Sin Limite postpaid plan remains the group's core mobile product in Mexico, with unlimited voice, data bundles, and included streaming perks. The date of this announcement is 16th June 2026, and it serves as a key window for US investors into how America Movil monetizes higher-value subscribers in its home market.

Telcel continues to leverage its Max Sin Limite postpaid plan family as a central tool for retaining higher-value customers. The plans combine unlimited talk and text across Mexico, the US, and Canada, along with sizable mobile data allowances and bundled app access. Currently, Max Sin Limite packages start at approximately MXN 399 per month, scaling up with larger data allowances and more generous streaming and social media benefits, effectively segmenting the market by usage intensity.

The Max Sin Limite concept is built around unlimited voice and SMS in Mexico, with roaming services in the US and Canada. Each plan offers a monthly high-speed data allowance that varies from single-digit gigabytes to significantly higher volumes for heavy users. Certain apps, including popular social networks, do not count toward the primary data bucket or come with additional dedicated data, making the plans more attractive for customers who consistently use these services. This strategy ties the commercial offer to America Movil's ongoing investments in mobile infrastructure.

From a customer perspective, the simplicity of a flat-fee structure with unlimited calling across North America reduces bill shock for cross-border workers and frequent travelers, providing predictable monthly costs for connectivity. Higher-end Max Sin Limite tiers also include value-added services such as additional cloud storage and discounts on handset financing, positioning the plans as a comprehensive bundle rather than just a connectivity service. This bundling strategy is vital for America Movil to differentiate Telcel in a competitive Mexican mobile market that includes AT&T and Telefonica's Movistar.

Industry observers note that Telcel's Max Sin Limite offerings align with America Movil's broader convergence push, where mobile, fixed broadband, and pay TV services are increasingly marketed together. The growing fiber footprint in Mexico allows for cross-selling mobile plans to existing fixed-line customers, enhancing revenue per household. Analysts emphasize the importance of postpaid and convergent offerings in stabilizing overall revenue for America Movil, especially as the company expands its 5G coverage and explores new digital services.

May 27, 2026: America Movil Charts Steady Growth Path with $7 Billion Capex Plan

MEXICO CITY - Mexican telecommunications giant America Movil on Wednesday outlined its financial outlook through 2028, targeting steady growth in revenue and core earnings while holding capital expenditure stable at around $7 billion per year. This information was shared during the company's investor day event, which took place on 27th May 2026, in New York.

During the presentation, America Movil projected that its revenue from services will grow by an average of 4.0% to 5.0% each year from 2026 to 2028. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) are expected to increase between 4.5% and 6.0% annually over the same period. The firm believes that a stable capital expenditure plan will support these growth targets.

The Latin American market leader plans to maintain its capital spending at approximately $7 billion per year, totaling $21 billion over the three-year period. Executives noted that this level of investment is feasible as the company has largely completed its significant purchases of radio frequencies necessary for its 5G network rollout.

The stable spending plan is designed to generate substantial cash, which America Movil intends to utilize for acquisitions, debt reduction, and returning value to investors. The company's executives confirmed they are actively seeking acquisition opportunities, particularly among struggling internet providers in Brazil and telecom operators in Eastern Europe, including Serbia and Slovenia.

For key markets like Brazil and Colombia, management expressed an aspiration to 'join the club of 50,' referring to a long-term goal of achieving a 50% profit margin. This ambitious target underscores America Movil's commitment to enhancing its operational efficiency and market position in the competitive telecommunications landscape.
