SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 10th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 10th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 10th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 10th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Its core business activities focus on the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger handling, cargo services, commercial concessions, and real estate development. SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte, S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a network of 13 airports primarily in the north-central region, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business activities focus on the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger handling, cargo services, commercial concessions, and real estate development. The company generates revenue through aeronautical fees, such as landing and parking charges, as well as non-aeronautical sources like retail, advertising, and parking. Among its fastest-growing segments are international passenger traffic, fueled by rising tourism and business travel, and cargo operations, which have expanded due to e-commerce and cross-border trade. OMA's strategic investments in modernization and expansion have enhanced operational efficiency, supporting sustained growth in a recovering aviation market. This positions the company as a vital contributor to Mexico's transportation infrastructure and economic connectivity. It is Mexico's 4th largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

5.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. SECTION 6 CORPORATE PROFILE

6.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

6.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 6 CORPORATE PROFILE

6.1 Activities

Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. (PINFRA), is a leading Mexican company specializing in the development, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure assets. Its core business activities encompass the management of toll road concessions, airport operations, and railway systems, primarily in Mexico, with a focus on enhancing connectivity and efficiency in transportation networks. The company has diversified into complementary areas such as industrial and urban infrastructure projects, leveraging public-private partnerships to drive growth. Among its fastest-growing segments are toll road concessions, fueled by increasing vehicular traffic and strategic expansions, as well as airport operations, which have benefited from rising passenger volumes and modernization efforts. PINFRA's commitment to sustainable practices and operational excellence positions it as a key player in Mexico's infrastructure sector, supporting economic development through reliable and innovative solutions. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 9th largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

8.1 Profiles of Board of Directors

Moises Ruben Kolteniuk Toyber

Director

Mr. Moises Ruben Kolteniuk Toyber serves as Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. In the past, he worked in the mining sector, within the Federal Government, as well as he has been Advisor of the mining area. Additionally, he served as Member of the Board of Directors of Aeropuertos del Sureste. He holds a degree in Electromechanical Engineering from Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico and a Masters degree in Operations Research from the University of California at Berkeley.

Adriana Graciela Penaloza Alanis

Director

Ms. Adriana Graciela Penaloza Alanis serves as Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. She has worked at Coordinacion Aplicada SA in the area of purchases, human resources, marketing management and international public relations. She holds a Bachelors degree in Graphics Design from Universidad Iberoamericana and a Masters degree in History of Art from Universidad Anahuac.

Luis Javier Solloa Hernandez

Independent Director

Mr. Luis Javier Solloa Hernandez serves as Independent Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. He is Chairman of the Company's Audit Committee and Member of the Corporate Practices Committee. He is also Associate Partner of the firm Solloa, Tello de Meneses y Compania SC. In addition, he has been Commissioner and Member of the Board of Directors of various companies within the industrial, commercial and financial sectors. He holds a degree in Public Accounting from Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico, a diploma in Financial Engineering from Colegio de Contadores Publicos de Mexico and a diploma in High Management from Universidad Iberoamericana.

Luis Hoyo Garcia

Independent Director

Mr. Luis Hoyo Garcia serves as Independent Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. He is Member of the Company's Audit Committee and Chairman of the Corporate Practices Committee. He has also been Chief Executive Officer of Agencia Aduanal Luis Hoyo and Chairman of Association of Duty Agents in Lazaro Cardenas, Michoacan. He graduated in Public Accounting from Universidad Anahuac.

Frantz Joseph Guns Devos

Independent Director

Mr. Frantz Joseph Guns Devos serves as Independent Director of Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura, S.A.B. de C.V. He has worked at Aeropuertos del Sureste, Infraestructura Portuaria Mexicana and Ferrocarriles del Sureste. He has also been Consultant in the areas of project management, strategic planning and corporate government. He holds a Bachelors degree in Applied Economics from Universitaire Faculteiten Sint-Ignatius Antwerp (UFSIA).

Breve resumen de la operación

Potencial adquisición de una participación adicional de 3.6778165% en los derechos fideicomisarios del Fideicomiso Promovido con los recursos de una Oferta Global de Certificados Bursátiles Fiduciarios de Inversión en Energía e Infraestructura Serie A identificados con clave de pizarra "FCFE 18" ("CBFEs Serie A), consistente en una oferta pública primaria subsecuente de suscripción y pago de CBFEs a realizarse en México (tanto de CBFEs Serie A entre el público inversionista, como CBFEs Serie B, para adquisición exclusiva por CFE), a través de la BMV (la "Oferta en México"), y una oferta privada primaria subsecuente de CBFEs Serie A a realizarse en los Estados Unidos de América y en otros mercados del extranjero al amparo de la Regla 144A (Rule 144A) y de la Regulación S (Regulation S) de la Ley de Valores de 1933 (Securities Act of 1933) de los Estados Unidos de América y de las demás disposiciones que resulten aplicables en los mercados donde tenga lugar la oferta internacional (la "Oferta Internacional"; la Oferta Internacional junto con la Oferta en México, la "Oferta Global"). La Oferta en México y la Oferta Internacional se realizarán simultáneamente.

A través de los recursos que se obtengan de Emisiones Adicionales de CBFEs, CFE Fibra E podría incrementar su participación económica en dichos derechos, que actualmente se encuentra en 9.5075% del Fideicomiso Promovido, y ampliar su exposición a este mediante la tenencia de Derechos Fideicomisarios, obteniendo el derecho a los flujos derivados de las Distribuciones que realice el Fideicomiso Promovido inmediatamente después de cualquiera de los incrementos de tenencia de Derechos Fideicomisarios.

.Características de los Títulos

La Oferta Global y la adquisición de derechos fideicomisarios contemplada en este Folleto Informativo sobre Reestructura Societaria, no afectará las características de los certificados bursátiles fiduciarios inmobiliarios con clave de pizarra "FCFE18" (CBFEs Serie A) y "FCFE18-2" (CBFEs Serie B) o a los derechos que los mismos confieren a sus Tenedores, excepto por potencialmente el precio y el número total de CBFEs en circulación.

Respecto al número de CBFEs en circulación y/o a ser emitidos una vez concluida la Oferta Global, dicho número podrá variar dependiendo de la o las Ofertas que se lleven a cabo para la consecución de la Oferta Global, así como las condiciones y evolución de las mismas. En el entendido de que la CFE mantendrá el 25% de los CBFEs en circulación a través de la Serie B, de conformidad con lo establecido en el Contrato de Fideicomiso.

A la fecha del presente Folleto Informativo hay 1,137,593,882 CBFEs CFE Fibra E en circulación, correspondientes a 853,195,411 CBFEs Serie A y 284,398,471 CBFEs Serie B. A la fecha no existe ningún CBFE en tesorería, ni se prevé que exista alguno después de la operación.

  5. Nombre comercial: FCFE18

  7. Lugar de constitución: Ciudad de México

Fideicomitente y Administrador

CFECapital, S. de R.L. de C.V.

Av. Paseo de la Reforma 412, Piso 4, Col. Juárez, C.P. 06600, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México, México.

Institución Fiduciaria

Banco Citi México, S.A., Institución de Banca Múltiple, Grupo Financiero Citi México. Administrador: CFE Capital, S. de R.L. de C.V.

Domicilio del Fiduciario

Avenida Revolución No 1267, Piso 11, Col. Los Alpes,

C.P. 01010 Álvaro Obregón, Ciudad de México, México.

Clave de pizarra: "FCFE18" (CBFEs Serie A) y "FCFE18-2" (CBFEs Serie B)

Presentado de conformidad con el artículo 35 de las Disposiciones de Carácter General Aplicables a las Emisoras de Valores y otros participantes del Mercado de Valores.

Breve resumen de la operación

Potencial adquisición de una participación adicional de 3.6778165% en los derechos fideicomisarios del Fideicomiso Promovido con los recursos de una Oferta Global de Certificados Bursátiles Fiduciarios de Inversión en Energía e Infraestructura Serie A identificados con clave de pizarra "FCFE 18" ("CBFEs Serie A), consistente en una oferta pública primaria subsecuente de suscripción y pago de CBFEs a realizarse en México (tanto de CBFEs Serie A entre el público inversionista, como CBFEs Serie B, para adquisición exclusiva por CFE), a través de la BMV (la "Oferta en México"), y una oferta privada primaria subsecuente de CBFEs Serie A a realizarse en los Estados Unidos de América y en otros mercados del extranjero al amparo de la Regla 144A (Rule 144A) y de la Regulación S (Regulation S) de la Ley de Valores de 1933 (Securities Act of 1933) de los Estados Unidos de América y de las demás disposiciones que resulten aplicables en los mercados donde tenga lugar la oferta internacional (la "Oferta Internacional"; la Oferta Internacional junto con la Oferta en México, la "Oferta Global"). La Oferta en México y la Oferta Internacional se realizarán simultáneamente.

A través de los recursos que se obtengan de Emisiones Adicionales de CBFEs, CFE Fibra E podría incrementar su participación económica en dichos derechos, que actualmente se encuentra en 9.5075% del Fideicomiso Promovido, y ampliar su exposición a este mediante la tenencia de Derechos Fideicomisarios, obteniendo el derecho a los flujos derivados de las Distribuciones que realice el Fideicomiso Promovido inmediatamente después de cualquiera de los incrementos de tenencia de Derechos Fideicomisarios.

.Características de los Títulos

La Oferta Global y la adquisición de derechos fideicomisarios contemplada en este Folleto Informativo sobre Reestructura Societaria, no afectará las características de los certificados bursátiles fiduciarios inmobiliarios con clave de pizarra "FCFE18" (CBFEs Serie A) y "FCFE18-2" (CBFEs Serie B) o a los derechos que los mismos confieren a sus Tenedores, excepto por potencialmente el precio y el número total de CBFEs en circulación.

Respecto al número de CBFEs en circulación y/o a ser emitidos una vez concluida la Oferta Global, dicho número podrá variar dependiendo de la o las Ofertas que se lleven a cabo para la consecución de la Oferta Global, así como las condiciones y evolución de las mismas. En el entendido de que la CFE mantendrá el 25% de los CBFEs en circulación a través de la Serie B, de conformidad con lo establecido en el Contrato de Fideicomiso.

A la fecha del presente Folleto Informativo hay 1,137,593,882 CBFEs CFE Fibra E en circulación, correspondientes a 853,195,411 CBFEs Serie A y 284,398,471 CBFEs Serie B. A la fecha no existe ningún CBFE en tesorería, ni se prevé que exista alguno después de la operación.

Datos relativos al Contrato de Fideicomiso de la CFE Fibra E

•  Denominación social del Fideicomitente y Administrador: CFECAPITAL, S. DE R.L. DE C.V.

•  Denominación social del vehículo administrado: Fideicomiso Irrevocable 188156 denominado "CFE Fibra E"

•  Fideicomisarios en primer lugar: Los Tenedores de los CBFEs Serie A.

•  Fideicomisarios en segundo lugar: Los Tenedores de los CBFEs Serie B. El único Tenedor de CBFEs Serie B es y será CFE o cualquiera de sus subsidiarias y/o filiales en términos del Contrato de Fideicomiso.

•  Nombre comercial: FCFE18

•  Fecha: 07 de febrero de 2018

•  Lugar de constitución: Ciudad de México

•  Duración: El Contrato de Fideicomiso permanecerá en pleno vigor y efecto hasta que los Fines del Fideicomiso hayan sido satisfechos en su totalidad; no obstante, lo anterior, este Contrato no terminará hasta que todas las obligaciones pagaderas con fondos del Patrimonio del Fideicomiso hayan sido pagadas en su totalidad. El plazo del presente Contrato no podrá exceder del plazo de 50 (cincuenta) años contemplado en el Artículo 394 de la LGTOC.

•  Domicilio: Nuestra oficina principal se encuentra en el Paseo de la Reforma 164, Col. Juárez, 06600 Ciudad de México, México.

Para mayor información sobre el Fideicomiso de Administración y Fuente de Pago Número 80758, denominado Fideicomiso Promovido, ir a la sección 2.1 "Breve descripción de los participantes".

Los Certificados Bursátiles Fiduciarios de Inversión en Energía e Infraestructura de FCFE se encuentran inscritos en el Registro Nacional de Valores y tienen aptitud para cotizar en bolsa.

"La inscripción en el Registro Nacional de Valores no implica certificación sobre la bondad de los valores, la solvencia de la emisora o sobre la exactitud o veracidad de la información contenida en esta declaración ni convalida actos que, en su caso, hubieren sido realizados en contravención de las leyes".
